3. A Linux server stores authentication activities in a file named auth.log. The security administrator wants to create a Bash script to perform a basic security check.



File name: auth.log

Oct 1 10:00:01 server sshd[101]: Failed password for root from 192.168.1.10 port 4455 ssh2

Oct 1 10:01:03 server sshd[102]: Failed password for admin from 192.168.1.20 port 4456 ssh2

Oct 1 10:02:15 server sshd[103]: Accepted password for user1 from 192.168.1.30 port 4457 ssh2

Oct 1 10:03:25 server sshd[104]: Invalid user test from 192.168.1.40 port 4458 ssh2

Oct 1 10:04:30 server sshd[105]: Failed password for root from 192.168.1.10 port 4459 ssh2



Analyze the given auth.log file and write a shell script to perform a basic security investigation. The script should:

a) Check whether auth.log exists.

b) Check whether the file is readable.

c) Check whether the file is not empty.

d) Detect and display login attempts involving the root user.

e) Generate a report file named security_report.txt.

Explain how the script performs the security checks.

A cybersecurity analyst collected the following suspicious entries from a Linux system and saved them in a file named investigation.txt, which contains



/home/user/document.txt

/tmp/update.sh

/tmp/.hidden_malware

/var/www/html/shell.php

root 1600 crypto_miner

www-data 1455 nc -lvp 4444

User admin from 192.168.1.10 executed /tmp/update.sh

* * * * * /tmp/.update.sh



Analyze the suspicious entries in investigation.txt and write suitable Linux commands to perform the following tasks:

a) If a line starts with /var/www/html, replace that line with Malware found.

b) Detect suspicious process lines containing crypto_miner or nc.

c) Mask the IP address 192.168.1.10 as x.x.x.x.

d) Delete the line containing document.txt and display the remaining lines.
